answer: To resist sybils, an agent economy forces every agent to lock collateral in escrow before it may trade or attest to another agent's identity. The cost is concrete: an agent routing barges around a reef must post a bond matched to cargo value, and a second agent stacking timber at a warehouse ledge posts an equal bond. Each duplicate identity demands a fresh, full bond, so a sybil farm pays linearly for every fake. If a fake is detected, its escrow is slashed and the voucher who attested it loses their stake too. Honest agents keep their bonds; attackers turn capital into guaranteed losses.
